rationale: #918: a POINTER-RETURN macro-wrapped heading — `MACRO(ret*, name)(params){ body }`. When the macro's first argument is a pointer type the grammar does NOT orphan the body (that is #917's spelling); it accepts the heading as a `function_definition` whose `type` field is a `macro_type_specifier` holding BOTH macro arguments — the return type inside an `ERROR`-wrapped `type_descriptor` with an `abstract_pointer_declarator`, and the NAME as the specifier's LAST named child — with the PARAMETER list in the `declarator` field. The analyzer's declarator route looks for a `function_declarator`, so `CGD38`'s guard drops the node: the definition was never a symbol, its body never a Function scope, and five of the six measured names existed only as the `#define`d macro constant from the file's thunk block. MEASURED THROUGH THE PRODUCTION ENTRY, pre-fix vs post-fix, only `src/ast/real-c-analyzer.ts` differing. PRE-FIX symbols (9): cmpp_size_t@32, cmpp_rc_e@33, helperTarget@38, helper_alloc@39, fileScope@41, cmpp_value_ctl@76, plain_return@84, plain_proto@92, caller@95 — i.e. NONE of the five pointer-return headings was a symbol, and their bodies' calls were attributed to FILE SCOPE (`calls global->helperTarget@46/54/63/70`). POST-FIX: all five exist as `function` symbols with their scope, return type, parameters and range, and those four calls are re-attributed to the function that makes them. The three pointer spellings are pinned because each reads the heading's own structure, never the source line: `(void *, cmpp_malloc)` and `(char const *, cmpp_rc_cstr)` (the return type's words arrive as a `type_qualifier` beside the pointer in the same `type_descriptor`) and `(cmpp_b *, cmpp_b_borrow)` — a STRUCT pointer, whose return type's base is itself a `type_identifier`, which is why the NAME slot is pinned by POSITION (the specifier's last named child, AFTER the return-type ERROR) and never by node type. The DECLARATION spelling (`(void *, cmpp_mrealloc)(void * p, size_t n)`) is pinned in the real file's own context: `#ifdef __cplusplus / extern "C" {` opens a brace the C parse cannot close until the region ends, so recovery cuts the heading after the FIRST parameter and leaves the rest of the parameter list plus the body's opening in an `ERROR` child, with the region's closing brace as the declaration's next sibling — all four pieces are required by the rule, and the second parameter (`n:size_t`) is read from that ERROR's own identifiers. CONTROLS: `cmpp_value_ctl` is a VALUE-return heading (the #917 class — recovered by THAT rule, and the pointer rule must not claim it twice); `plain_return` is an ordinary pointer-returning function and `plain_proto` a pointer prototype (untouched); `cmpp_b_clear(void)` pins the UNNAMED parameter to `unknown`, so no fix can name a definition after a type word. The declaration spelling's CALL-SITE resolution is deliberately NOT pinned: the fixture defines it last (inside the `extern "C"` region the shape requires), so there is no call to resolve, and a forward unprototyped call would be a pin of something the fixture does not honestly contain. NOT pinned, and merely declared: `calls global->CMPP__EXPORT@76` is the call-shaped reading of the macro INVOCATION itself — measured IDENTICAL pre-fix and post-fix, a pre-existing artifact of the same grammar accident (#917 documents it in its own fixture), so it is not enshrined here and not forbidden either.

forbidParameters.note: the unnamed-parameter contract: a lone type word is `unknown`, never the parameter's name — and the declared NAME is never taken from the type.
